chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you enter into intimacy with your wife, take her by the nasa (forehead/hair), face the Qiblah, and say: 'O Allah, by Your trust I have taken her, and by Your words I have permitted her. So if You have decreed for me a child from her, make it blessed, pious, from the Shiah of the Family of Muhammad, and do not make for Satan any share or portion in it.'

key_terms.بِنَاصِيَتِهَا: by the forehead/hair (a gesture of taking possession or intimacy)
key_terms.شِيعَةِ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Shiah of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and etiquette during marital intimacy in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Abu Basir, emphasizing the spiritualization of marital relations by treating them as an act of worship (ibadah) rather than mere physical gratification. The instruction to hold the 'forehead' (nasiyah) and face the Qiblah symbolizes grounding the physical act in divine presence and trust (amanah), while the supplication specifically seeks offspring who are not only pious but also distinctively aligned with the Shia identity of the Ahl al-Bayt, guarding them against the influence of Shaytan.
